semiMajorAxis_desc: Mean distance of the satellite from the ellipse focal point
eccentricity_desc: Elongation degree of the orbital ellipse (0 is circular)
primaryMassFactor_desc: Mass of central planet in Earth mass multiples (M⊕)
satelliteMass_desc: Mass of the orbiting payload or probe
atmosphericDrag_real: In real mode, upper atmospheric drag at perigee bleeds specific orbital energy leading to decay
formula_vis_viva: Vis-Viva Equation for Instantaneous Orbital Speed
formula_kepler_third: Kepler's Third Law of Orbital Periods
theoryContent:
Kepler's Three Laws of Orbital Motion:
1. The orbit of a planet/satellite is an ellipse with the primary at one of the two foci.
2. A line segment joining the satellite and primary sweeps out equal areas during equal intervals of time (conservation of angular momentum).
3. The square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis (T² ∝ a³).
Orbital speed reaches its maximum at periapsis and minimum at apoapsis, governed by the Vis-Viva equation.
